readout_other: Ca2+ imaging (OGD-488, GCaMP6f); whole-cell patch clamp; mCherry thermometry
direction_notes: Photoacoustic pulse trains evoked Ca2+ responses, subthreshold depolarisations and action potentials in cultured cortical neurons, at about 1/40 of the laser energy needed for photothermal stimulation.
safety_notes: Temperature rise on neurons under photoacoustic conditions was negligible by mCherry fluorescence.

exposures.label: Photoacoustic fiber emitter (candle soot/PDMS) driven by ns pulsed laser

device.model: Fiber emitter: 200 um optical fiber tip coated with candle soot and PDMS, driven by a 1030 nm 3 ns laser

timing.protocol_description: Nanosecond laser pulses (3 ns, 1030 nm) at 4.23 kHz repetition rate for Ca imaging (1.7 kHz in the ion-channel experiments) delivered as 1.5 ms or 3 ms bursts, average laser power 120 mW, fiber tip about 50 um from the neurons. Photothermal comparison used a CW 1064 nm laser for 10 to 100 ms.

source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: Under the laser condition of 45 μJ per pulse, the FE produced an ultrasound waveform with a peak-to-peak pressure of over 8 MPa
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: We estimated the pressure generated by the FE is 5 MPa, based on the laser pulse energy.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: A 3 ns pulsed laser at 1030 nm and a 1.7 kHz repetition rate was used to deliver laser pulses of 3 ms duration to a FE with a 100 μm tip diameter (Figure 5f).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Dark pink: pulsed laser with 5 pulses in 1.5 ms. Red: pulsed laser with 11 pulses in 3 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: the tip of a commercial optical fiber with a diameter of 200 μm was coated with a layer of candle soot, as an absorber, and a second layer ofpolydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)
